duplicate_screen.base_search: Sangjeong / Sangjong / Sangjŏng across discoveries and leads returned no match at named base.
duplicate_screen.comparison: Jikji metal-type record concerns the surviving 1377 Buddhist text, with archaeological evidence and availability and donation events; Jikji woodblock concerns the different 1378 edition. The proposed earlier Sangjeong ritual-text edition is a distinct subject and reported publication, not either existing event. No continuity is inferred.

evidence_limitations: Accounts are not independent physical witnesses, and both rely on historical literature; no original postface or surviving Sangjeong printing was examined.

The museum dates the postface around 1234, while the article estimates printing 1234–1241. These are approximate attributions with potentially different dating assumptions; do not present either as a precise proven bound or claim that the postface necessarily postdates every possible date in the estimate. Original witness and chronology require research.
The article also makes a disputed claim about another book; this review accepts none of that claim.
No origin, priority, causal relation, transmission, funder or place coordinates are accepted. Existing records and claims are outside this review.
